root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `selected_curve == nettle_get_gost_gc256b()` before the returned pointer is consumed by `ecc_point_init(&r, curve)` for `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPA`, `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPXA`, and `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256B`.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: The three 256-bit GOST cases must dispatch to the GC256B curve object whose layout matches the external Nettle `struct ecc_curve` consumed by `ecc_mul_g` and `sec_tabselect`.
root_cause_criterion.description: Vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` aliases the witnessed 256-bit GOST enum set to the local `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` backport instead of the GC256B curve object expected by external Nettle, so the returned pointer later exposes the wrong tail fields under the external layout.

nodes.state: At the sink-side `p[i]` load, the first read that leaves the aliased table base occurs at `&p[i] == table + (rn / 2)`, the first limb beyond the extent of the aliased `ecc_unit` object.

edges.relation: The pointer selected by `get_supported_gost_curve()` is stored unchanged in `r.ecc` after `ecc_point_init(&r, curve)`.
The same `r.ecc` pointer is later loaded as the `ecc` argument consumed by external `ecc_mul_g()`.
The bogus table base computed from `ecc->pippenger_table` is passed unchanged as `sec_tabselect()`'s `table` argument.
